topic: AI Agent Security Best Practices 2026: Beyond Prompt Injection

competitors.title: Build Agents You Can Trust Across Any Framework With Open Evals and a Control Standard (Microsoft Build 2026)
key_points: Microsoft announced ASSERT (Adaptive Spec-driven Scoring for Evaluation and Regression Testing): open-source policy-driven evaluation framework for AI agents
Agent Control Specification (ACS): portable runtime control standard as part of Agent Governance Toolkit — the MCP/A2A equivalent for agent safety
ACS defines 5 validation checkpoints: input, LLM, state, tool execution, and output with deterministic control logic
Written policies don't translate into working runtime controls — critical gap in agent production deployment
ASSERT converts organizational policies into concrete, measurable evaluations with context-specific test cases
ACS expressed as standard policy YAML — portable, versionable, and auditable
Foundry's Guided Guardrail Setup gives personalized guardrail recommendations from a short questionnaire
Runtime Data Loss Prevention extends Microsoft Purview into agent interactions for real-time sensitive data blocking
Partners include CrewAI, Arize AI, LiteLLM, Pydantic, IBM, KPMG, Zscaler

competitors.title: Best Practices for Deploying AI Agents in Production: Architecture, Rollout, and Governance Checklist (Cordum)
key_points: Production AI agents need 8 things in order: threat model, pre-dispatch policy enforcement, approval workflows, least-privilege scoping, output safety, audit trails, staged rollout (5%→25%→50%→100%), tested rollback drills
Highest-leverage control is pre-dispatch policy enforcement — deterministic decision point before the agent acts
In-process vs out-of-process governance: latter increasingly the audit expectation for regulated deployments
Staged rollout with objective gates: error budget, policy-decision latency p99, approval turnaround time, rollback-drill success
Four decision types: ALLOW, DENY, REQUIRE_APPROVAL, ALLOW_WITH_CONSTRAINTS
Three failure modes: no decision boundary, no staged rollout, no incident narrative
Six-layer production stack: Execution Bus, State & Pointers, Scheduler, Policy Decision Point, Output Safety, Audit Trail
Phase 0: Synthetic + replay, Phase 1: 5% low-risk, Phase 2: 25% mixed, Phase 3: 50-100% with objective gates

competitors.title: AI Agents in Production: A Complete Deployment Guide for 2026 (Dev Stars)
key_points: Three fundamental production challenges: non-determinism, tool use risk, long-horizon failure cascades
Supervisor-Worker pattern with scoped tool access reduces blast radius per worker
Reflection loops before irreversible actions with confidence thresholds
Safety guardrails: Pydantic input validation, hard caps (max_steps=20), tool permission allowlists
CostGuard pattern: rate limiting with token budgets per hour for cost control
Infinite loop detection via state hashing and sliding window memory
OpenTelemetry instrumentation for every LLM call with structured logging
Containerization: isolated containers, non-root user, no default network

competitors.title: AI Agent Frameworks in 2026: 8 SDKs and Built-in Guardrail Mechanisms (MorphLLM)
key_points: 8 frameworks compared with built-in guardrail mechanisms: Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK, LangGraph, CrewAI, Smolagents, Pydantic AI, AutoGen
OpenAI Agents SDK: three-tier guardrails (input/output/tool) with lightweight architecture
Claude Agent SDK: deepest MCP integration with hooks system for custom guardrail logic
Pydantic AI: type-safe structured output validation as guardrail mechanism
Framework choice defines your guardrail architecture — provider-native vs independent frameworks

competitors.title: Definitive Guide to Agentic Frameworks in 2026 (Softmax Data)
key_points: LangGraph v1.1.3: deep agent templates, distributed runtime CLI, 25K GitHub stars
CrewAI v1.12: agent skills, native OpenAI-compatible providers, Qdrant Edge memory, 44.6K stars
OpenAI Agents SDK v0.13: any-LLM adapter, opt-in retry policies, MCP resource support, session persistence
AG2 Beta: ground-up redesign with streaming event-driven architecture, multi-provider support
Pydantic AI v1.71: Capabilities (composable agent behaviors), AgentSpec YAML/JSON loading
Google ADK v2.0.0-alpha: graph-based workflow runtime, Task API for agent-to-agent delegation
